decisions.rationale: Rotom-Wash + Incineroar lead: Rotom-Wash threatens Palafin/Toxapex/Glimmora with Electric/Water STAB; Incineroar's Fake Out breaks Mimikyu's Disguise, Intimidate weakens physical attackers, Flare Blitz destroys Meowscarada/Aegislash. Dragapult in back provides speed, Shadow Ball for Mimikyu/Aegislash, Thunderbolt for Palafin/Toxapex. Metagross-Mega cleans with Tough Claws Steel moves into Mimikyu/Glimmora and Bullet Punch priority.

Mimikyu leads safely behind Disguise, threatening Dragapult and Mega Metagross with PlayRough and providing priority Shadow Sneak. Meowscarada supplies essential speed control at 192 Speed with Protean-boosted coverage, enabling revenge kills against Dragapult and opposing sweepers. Aegislash is the dedicated Mega counter—its Mega form's Tough Claws-boosted Sacred Sword and Shadow Ball pressure Mega Metagross directly, while King's Shield punishes physical attackers. Toxapex rounds out the squad as a Regenerator physical wall that absorbs Incineroar's attacks and pivots with Recover, giving the team a reliable defensive backbone.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Mega Metagross, Dragapult, Incineroar pivot. Dual hazards via Glimmora Toxic Debris. Lum Berry + Sitrus Berry sustain. Intimidate + Parting Shot weakens physical attackers and pivots safely. Mimikyu Disguise is single-use—save for a high-impact threat. Own Mega Evolution (Aegislash) is critical to answering Mega Metagross. Speed control through Meowscarada is the primary tempo tool. No hazard removal available—avoid unnecessary early switches.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out on Meowscarada prevents it from hitting Rotom-Wash with a super-effective Grass move (Energy Ball/Flower Trick) while Meowscarada is faster. Volt Switch on Mimikyu breaks Disguise and pivots Rotom-Wash out to a better matchup like Dragapult, who threatens both foes with Shadow Ball. Even if Meowscarada Protects, Disguise still breaks and Rotom pivots safely.
decisions.notebook: Opponent tendencies: Led Palafin + Mimikyu Game 1, switched to Mimikyu + Meowscarada Game 2. Adapts leads between games. Mimikyu carries Focus Sash + Disguise; needs two hits to KO. Meowscarada is mixed with Expert Belt and Protean, threatens Rotom-Wash with Grass moves. Glimmora, Toxapex, Aegislash, Palafin not yet revealed Game 2; two of them are in the back. Future plan: Break Disguise early, preserve Rotom-Wash for Meowscarada matchup, use Dragapult's Shadow Ball to pressure Mimikyu post-Disguise.

decisions.rationale: Switch Rotom-Wash to Dragapult to preserve the Electric/Water pivot while gaining a fast Ghost/Dragon that outspeeds both foes. Dragapult resists Meowscarada's likely Grass move (Energy Ball 16-25%, Flower Trick 11-16%) and is immune to Brick Break. The main risk is Dark Pulse (70-110% possible OHKO), but the opponent must predict the switch; if they instead target Rotom's slot with Grass, Dragapult takes minimal damage and threatens both foes next turn with Life Orb Shadow Ball (72-132% on 87% Mimikyu, Focus Sash already consumed) and Draco Meteor (72-140% on 75% Meowscarada). Incineroar has only Pass available.
decisions.notebook: Opponent tendencies: Led Palafin + Mimikyu Game 1, switched to Mimikyu + Meowscarada Game 2. Adapts leads between games. Mimikyu carries Focus Sash + Disguise; needs two hits to KO — Disguise now broken. Meowscarada is mixed with Expert Belt and Protean, threatens Rotom-Wash with Grass moves. Glimmora, Toxapex, Aegislash, Palafin not yet revealed Game 2; two of them are in the back. Future plan: Dragapult's Shadow Ball pressures Mimikyu post-Disguise; Incineroar's Flare Blitz OHKOs Meowscarada; preserve Rotom-Wash for favorable matchups; Metagross-Mega is a late-game win condition with Tough Claws Bullet Punch.

decisions.rationale: Both attackers target Rotom-Wash to eliminate a key pivot before it can act. Mimikyu's Shadow Sneak (Ghost +1 priority) hits neutrally and moves first, while Meowscarada's Energy Ball (Grass, super effective 2x) exploits the Water typing for heavy damage. Combining both offenses maximizes the chance of a KO on the faster foe, removing a dangerous Electric/Water pivot and maintaining tempo. Mimikyu's Disguise is preserved for a bigger incoming threat, and Aegislash stays benched for the future Mega Metagross matchup.

Mimikyu Disguise single-use—save for high-impact physical threat. Aegislash Mega critical for Mega Metagross. Speed control through Meowscarada is primary tempo tool. No hazard removal—minimize early switches. Intimidate already active on both my physical attackers.

decisions.rationale: Dragapult Protect shields it from Meowscarada's Dark Pulse (70.6-110.4%, possible OHKO) and Mimikyu's attacks. Incineroar Flare Blitz guarantees the KO on Meowscarada (83.1-160.3% from 75% HP). Even if both foes target Incineroar, worst-case damage is Brick Break (40.6%) + Play Rough (25.7%) = 66.3%, which Incineroar easily survives. This eliminates the biggest threat (Meowscarada) while preserving Dragapult for the 2v1 against Mimikyu and the unrevealed back line.

Both Pokémon target Dragapult, the fastest and most dangerous remaining foe. Mimikyu-Busted uses priority Shadow Sneak (Ghost, +1, SE 2x) to hit before Dragapult can act, while Meowscarada fires Dark Pulse (SE 2x) for strong neutral-damage pressure. Eliminating Dragapult removes the opponent's primary speed and offensive threat, giving you tempo control with Meowscarada for the rest of the game.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Mega Metagross, Dragapult, Incineroar pivot. Dual hazards via Glimmora Toxic Debris. Lum Berry + Sitrus Berry sustain. Mimikyu Disguise single-use—already expended. Aegislash Mega critical for Mega Metagross matchup. Speed control through Meowscarada is primary tempo tool. No hazard removal—minimize early switches. Intimidate already active on both physical attackers. Prioritize eliminating Dragapult to secure tempo advantage.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex walls both Dragapult and Incineroar effectively—Dragapult's Shadow Ball and Draco Meteor are resisted, and Incineroar's Flare Blitz and Fake Out are also resisted. Regenerator plus Recover plus Leftovers gives excellent staying power, letting Mimikyu-Busted safely use priority Shadow Sneak to pressure Dragapult. Saving Aegislash for the anticipated Mega Metagross matchup preserves the notebook's critical late-game asset. Mimikyu stays in to fire another priority Shadow Sneak before Dragapult can act.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Mega Metagross, Dragapult, Incineroar pivot. Dual hazards via Glimmora Toxic Debris. Lum Berry + Sitrus Berry sustain. Mimikyu Disguise expended. Aegislash Mega critical for Mega Metagross matchup. Speed control through Meowscarada lost—Toxapex now provides defensive backbone. No hazard removal—minimize early switches. Intimidate already active on both physical attackers. Prioritize eliminating Dragapult to secure tempo advantage. Toxapex on field as Regenerator wall; preserve Aegislash for Metagross.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Mimikyu to guarantee the KO through Focus Sash. Dragapult's Shadow Ball (72–132%) either breaks Sash leaving Mimikyu at 1 HP or leaves it at ~15%; Incineroar's Flare Blitz (43–83%) always finishes it regardless. Mimikyu is the biggest threat with SwordsDance + priority Shadow Sneak that could snowball if left alive. Toxapex gets one free action — worst case is Toxic on Dragapult — but removing Mimikyu now is worth that cost. The Speed order is Dragapult → Mimikyu → (Incineroar/Toxapex speed tie), but Flare Blitz KOs Mimikyu either before or after Toxapex moves.

Mimikyu-Busted is the only Pokémon that safely walls Dragapult (Draco Meteor immune, Shadow Ball resisted) and must press that advantage immediately with Play Rough for heavy neutral-bonus damage before likely being KO'd by Dragapult's Shadow Ball. Toxapex applies Toxic on Dragapult to stack residual with Mimikyu's chip, accelerating the elimination of the series' most dangerous foe.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Mega Metagross, Dragapult, Incineroar pivot. Dual hazards via Glimmora Toxic Debris. Lum Berry + Sitrus Berry sustain. Mimikyu Disguise expended. Aegislash Mega critical for Mega Metagross matchup. Dragapult is priority elimination target. After this turn, bring Aegislash against Metagross.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Dragapult Protects to safely avoid Aegislash's guaranteed-OHKO Shadow Ball. Incineroar uses Parting Shot into Aegislash: as a non-damaging status move it bypasses King's Shield, lowering Aegislash's Atk/SpA by 1 and pivoting Incineroar out. This neuters Aegislash's offensive threat while preserving both of our Pokémon and bringing in a fresh back-line member.

Dragapult stays in to pressure Aegislash with Shadow Ball (51.5-92.6%, 2HKO range) and Toxapex with Thunderbolt. Incineroar's Parting Shot switch brings Rotom-Wash, which threatens Toxapex with super-effective Electric STAB, resists Liquidation (7.6-19.2%), takes Aegislash Shadow Ball neutrally (19.7-36.8%), and can Volt Switch later to regain momentum. Metagross-Mega is strong but Rotom-Wash's type matchups are cleaner here: it isn't weak to any foe move and has reliable 100%-accurate Thunderbolt vs Toxapex. Opponent down to last two Pokémon with no bench; preserving Dragapult and Rotom-Wash while wearing them down is the safest path to close out game 2.

Aegislash's Shadow Ball is 2x super-effective against Dragapult (the priority elimination target) with a possible KO range of 59.5-111.7% on 90% HP. Even if Dragapult retaliates with Shadow Ball (51.1-75.9% damage), Aegislash survives at 24-49% HP. Toxapex's Liquidation is 2x super-effective against Incineroar (Fire/Water weakness), dealing 24.8-47.1% of max HP to the already-weakened 77% Incineroar. This maximizes offensive pressure to eliminate the top threat while keeping Aegislash alive for the Metagross matchup.

Double Thunderbolt into Toxapex guarantees a KO: Dragapult min 46.5% + Rotom min 53.5% = 100% ≥ Toxapex's 92% HP. Toxapex lacks Protect and the opponent has no bench, so this cannot be blocked. Aegislash's Shadow Ball does 55.2–78.5% to Dragapult, leaving it alive at 1.5–24.8% after Life Orb recoil. Next turn it's 2v1 against a -1 SpA Aegislash, which Dragapult Shadow Ball threatens to OHKO. Splitting attacks risks both foes surviving; focusing Aegislash leaves Toxapex free to Toxic Rotom. This line secures a knockout with minimal risk.

King's Shield (priority +4) protects Aegislash from Dragapult's likely super-effective Shadow Ball OHKO attempt and drops Dragapult's offenses by 2 if it attacks. Toxic on Dragapult starts residual chip damage on the priority elimination target. This keeps Aegislash alive and healthy for the upcoming Metagross matchup while steadily wearing down Dragapult.

Aegislash is the opponent's last Pokémon. Dragapult Shadow Ball (51.5–92.6%) + Rotom Thunderbolt (23.4–40.7%) gives a high probability OHKO (74.9–133.3% combined). Both moves are 100% accurate. Dragapult outspeeds Aegislash, so if the combined rolls KO, Aegislash never attacks. Even if we miss the KO range, we have two healthy backline Pokémon to clean up next turn. King's Shield has reduced success rate and doesn't punish special moves.

Shadow Ball on Dragapult is the only super-effective option against the priority elimination target, dealing 40-75% of its max HP. Even if Dragapult retaliates with Shadow Ball (51-76% to Aegislash), Aegislash survives and remains healthy enough for the planned Metagross matchup next turn. Toxapex is fainted so must pass.
decisions.notebook: Opponent core: Mega Metagross, Dragapult, Incineroar pivot. Dual hazards via Glimmora Toxic Debris. Lum Berry + Sitrus Berry sustain. Mimikyu Disguise expended. Aegislash Mega critical for Mega Metagross matchup. Dragapult heavily damaged this turn; follow up with Aegislash against Metagross next game.

reflections.summary: Our lead matchup and pivoting overwhelmed the opponent. Incineroar's Fake Out and Flare Blitz removed Meowscarada early, Rotom-Wash broke Mimikyu's Disguise and pivoted into Dragapult, which cleaned up with super effective Shadow Balls. The opponent's Toxapex and Aegislash couldn't withstand the special pressure. Between-game adjustments—continuing with Incineroar+Rotom lead and bringing Dragapult—worked perfectly against their adapted Mimikyu+Meowscarada lead. The series was won 2-0 due to superior team composition and clean execution.
reflections.adjustment: In a future series, consider a plan for Glimmora hazards, as our team lacks removal. Leading Dragapult or Metagross could pressure it early, or bring Gliscor if it has Defog. Otherwise, the Incineroar+Rotom lead remains strong, and preserving Incineroar's Lum Berry for Toxic is valuable.
reflections.notebook: Opponent tendencies: Adapts leads between games (Palafin+Mimikyu, Mimikyu+Meowscarada). May try Glimmora lead for hazards. Mimikyu: Focus Sash, Disguise, Swords Dance, Play Rough, Shadow Sneak, Shadow Ball, Jolly. Meowscarada: Expert Belt, Protean, Flower Trick, Dark Pulse, Energy Ball, Brick Break, Naive; Dark Pulse threatens Dragapult. Toxapex: Leftovers, Regenerator, Bold, Liquidation, Recover, Toxic, Haze; passive but spreads status. Aegislash: Shell Bell, Careful, King's Shield, Shadow Ball, Flash Cannon, Sacred Sword; King's Shield mindgames. Palafin: Life Orb, Zero to Hero, Jolly, Close Combat, Waterfall, Ice Beam, Flip Turn. Glimmora: Lum Berry, Toxic Debris, Timid, Stealth Rock, Spikes, Power Gem, Earth Power. Future plan: Incineroar's Fake Out+Flare Blitz handles Meowscarada; Rotom-Wash pivots and threatens Toxapex/Palafin; Dragapult's Shadow Ball/Thunderbolt pressures Mimikyu, Aegislash, and Palafin; Mega Metagross cleans late. Beware Meowscarada's Dark Pulse on Dragapult—use Protect or switch. Against Glimmora, apply immediate offense to deny hazards. Preserve Incineroar's Lum Berry for Toxic if possible.

reflections.summary: Lost 0-2. The opponent's Dragapult + Rotom-Wash Thunderbolt combination overwhelmed the team; every Water/Ground-type on my roster was 2HKO'd or OHKO'd by Electric coverage. Incineroar's Intimidate plus Parting Shot crippled Mimikyu and Aegislash before they could contribute offensively. Mimikyu's Disguise was burned on the switch to Rotom-Wash (Turn 1), eliminating the best revenge-killer. Aegislash entered after Parting Shot had already lowered its offenses, so it could never threaten. Toxapex was double-Thunderbolted and died. No team member survived long enough to mount a meaningful response. Between-game adjustments (saving Aegislash for Mega Metagross) were never tested because the series ended; the core problem—no Electric immunity and no pivot that could survive two fast special attackers firing super-effective moves—was never addressed.
reflections.adjustment: Swap Palafin and Glimmora slots for a Ground-type immune to Electric (e.g., Swampert with Earthquake/Earth Power/Protect/Flip Turn) and a faster offensive lead that can threaten Dragapult before it sets up (e.g., Spiritomb with Shadow Sneak/Trick to punish Choice items, or Torkoal under Drought to enable Meowscarada's Sun-boosted offenses and reduce Thunder accuracy). Prioritize keeping Mimikyu's Disguise intact by leading it against non-volatile-damage foes, or replace it entirely with the Ground pivot. Against this opponent's pivot-heavy, Electric-spam style, the priority is: (1) an Electric-immune pivot that can absorb hits and chip, (2) speed control or a faster revenge killer, and (3) hazard pressure to punish Dragapult's Life Orb recoil and Rotom's Sitrus recovery.
reflections.notebook: Opponent core tendencies: Dragapult runs mixed Life Orb set (Shadow Ball + Thunderbolt + Draco Meteor + Protect); Rotom-Wash is a Sitrus pivot with Thunderbolt/Volt Switch/Hydro Pump/Protect—both fire Thunderbolt at high accuracy for 2HKO on bulky Waters. Incineroar is an Intimidate + Parting Shot pivot with Lum Berry; it forces chip then pivots out to bring in wallbreakers safely. Opponent uses dual pivoting to maintain momentum and stack favorable matchups. Revealed: opponent values speed control via Parting Shot rather than Tailwind; Lum Berry consumed means Incineroar loses one-time safety next game. Hidden slot likely Mega Metagross (Expert Belt + Meteor Mash coverage) or Gliscor (Poison Heal + Swords Dance). Prep conclusions: bring Ground immunity, stack Electric resistance or evasion (Drought/rain), carry a fast lead that can threaten Dragapult before setup, and avoid relying on Mimikyu Disguise against Volt Switch/Parting Shot teams—it gets burned for free.
